info.bio:
Fleetwood Mac, grupo anglo-estadounidense de música blues rock. Creado a finales de los años 60 cambió su estilo de un blues tradicional como en el disco English Rose , a rock alternativo  y finalmente pop. Sus períodos más exitosos fueron en sus inicios, cuando entre sus fundadores figuraba Peter Green, y en los últimos años de la década de los setenta, cuando la voz de Stevie Nicks y las canciones de Lindsay Buckingham tuvieron mucho éxito.

Creada en 1967, en Londres por Peter Green (guitarra), Jeremy Spencer (guitarra), John McVie (bajo), Mick Fleetwood (batería), la banda inició su carrera interpretando blues durante un período de renacimiento que tuvo el estilo. Peter Green fue antes miembro de la legendaria banda de John Mayall donde también tocó John McVie. Publicaron los discos Peter Green's Fleetwood Mac, Mr. Wonderfull, English Rose y Pious Birds of Good Omen (álbum recopilatorio) y algunos de sus sencillos, como Black Magic Woman y la instrumental Albatross, estuvieron en los primeros puestos de las listas en Inglaterra.

En 1970 Jeremy Spencer deja la banda, se incorpora Danny Kirwan (guitarra) y publican Then Play On, un álbum experimental que los aleja del blues y los acerca al rock. Será el último trabajo de Green con el grupo y será también un momento de crisis para él y el resto de la banda. En 1970 se incorporarán Christine McVie (voz y teclados), esposa de John, y el guitarrista estadounidense Bob Welch. Publican con esta formación dos discos: Kiln House y Future Games. Ya alejados completamente del blues, siguen la experimentación y un acercamiento a un sonido más estadounidense, más cercano al country. Estos discos son mucho menos exitosos, quizás por lo lejos que están del gusto del público inglés y lo desconocidos que son para los estadounidenses.

Cuando en 1971 Kirwan deja la banda, por problemas personales, empienza un período de crisis que durará desde 1972 hasta 1975, en el cual publican discos con diferentes estilos y tendencias: Bare Trees (dark, lleno de melodías y letras oscuras), Mystery To Me (ligero), Penguin y Heroes Are Hard to Find (difíciles de clas), Fleetwood Mac Live (1980, grabado durante la gira mundial de promoción de Tusk) y Mirage (1982).

Todos estos discos fueron muy exitosos, aparecieron en las carteleras de los más escuchados en varias ocasiones y fueron disco de oro y plata en varios países. Rumours, junto a The Dark Side of the Moon de Pink Floyd, es uno de los discos más vendidos. En 1982, luego de una gira mundial, Fleetwood Mac pasa por otra crisis, se separan temporalmente y cada roduce discos en solitario, siendo Stevie Nicks la más popular. Un gran grupo.

scenes.name: Blues revival y blues-rock
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: John Mayall define con Bluesbreakers (con Eric Clapton) el rhythm'n'blues tocado por blancos europeos, el blues-rock, y siembra el progresivo con sus discos de jazz y lounge. Su equivalente americano es Al Kooper (Blues Project, Supersession, Blood Sweat & Tears). Cream, el primer power-trio, cambia la cara del rock británico con improvisación de jazz, distorsión y solos interminables; Fleetwood Mac de Peter Green y Ten Years After llevan del blues al hard rock. En San Francisco, Janis Joplin, Steve Miller y Santana; en Los Ángeles, Taj Mahal y Ry Cooder reconstruyen las tradiciones; Bob Seger casa el grito soul con el Detroit obrero.

scenes.name: Techno-rock y pop de estudio
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El «sonido» por encima de la melodía, el ritmo y la armonía: Electric Light Orchestra inventa el «high-tech pop»; Supertramp, Alan Parsons Project, Kansas, Styx y Split Enz. El valor de la producción define a Steely Dan (el pop-jazz pulido de los yuppies), Hall & Oates, los Fleetwood Mac de Rumours y Tusk, Toto, el «muro de sonido» titánico de Jim Steinman (Bat Out Of Hell) y la Penguin Cafe Orchestra. A finales de los setenta, el art-rock culmina en los supergrupos: 10cc, Godley & Creme, Foreigner, UK, Asia, Sky.

scenes.name: Brit-pop y post-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Como tantas veces, el fenómeno más publicitado es el menos interesante: un «brit-pop» de grupos terriblemente parecidos y tediosos, sin apenas imaginación. Lo anticipan Lightning Seeds, La's, Teenage Fanclub y Heavenly; estalla con Boo Radleys, Blur (Parklife) y Oasis (el «farol» que mejor personifica la moda). Suede y el glam-pop (Super Furry Animals, Placebo), las excepciones de High Llamas (Hawaii) y Supergrass, el revival mod (Ocean Colour Scene, Wildhearts), Elastica, Sleeper, las Spice Girls; Trembling Blue Stars, Tindersticks, Delgados. El post-pop de Radiohead, «la banda más publicitada y sobrevalorada de la década», cuyo OK Computer es una obra maestra del falso vanguardismo; Coldplay, Travis.

podcast.title: Danny Kirwan Fired - Violent Nervous Breakdown (1972)
podcast.body: After experiencing a violent nervous breakdown in the summer of 1972, Danny Kirwan was fired from Fleetwood Mac. This left Bob Welch and Christine McVie to assume primary songwriting duties and further expand the band's sound. "After a violent nervous breakdown in the summer of 72, Danny Kerwin was fired."

podcast.title: Move to Los Angeles - 1974
podcast.body: In 1974, Fleetwood Mac attempted a change of scenery by moving from London to record in Los Angeles. This move coincided with a shift in their sound, with Christine McVie quickly adapting her songwriting to incorporate American-style pop elements. "In 1974, the band tried a change of scenery, moving from London to record in Los Angeles."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: 1975 Lineup Changes
podcast.body: In 1975, when Bob Welch left the band, Lindsey Buckingham was invited to join. Buckingham stipulated that his girlfriend, Stevie Nicks, also be accepted into the band. This led to American folk rock singer-songwriters Buckingham and Nicks joining Mick Fleetwood (drums), John McVie (bass), and Christine McVie (keyboards, singer-songwriter). "in 1975 Lindsey Buckingham insisted that his girlfriend Stevie Nicks be accepted into what remained of Fleetwood Mac at that time when Lindsey Buckingham was invited to fill the void. That was left when Bob Welch left the band so you have a pair of American folk rock singer songwriters Buckingham and Nicks joining the drummer Mick Fleetwood the bassist John McVee and keyboard player and singer songwriter Christine McVee yes John's wife."

podcast.title: Slow Rise to Number One - Fleetwood Mac (1975) Album
podcast.body: The 1975 self-titled Fleetwood Mac album achieved an unusual chart record for the longest climb to number one in Billboard album chart history up to that date, taking 58 weeks to reach the top. To this day, it ranks third for the slowest rise, trailing only the *O Brother, Where Art Thou?* soundtrack and a Kid Laroi album. "It was the longest climb to number one in Billboard album chart history to that date."

podcast.title: Album Rock Radio Dominance in 1977
podcast.body: By the end of 1977, nearly every song from the "Rumours" album, including "The Chain," "Second Hand News," "Gold Dust Woman," and the ballad "Songbird," became an FM staple on album rock radio. "on album rock radio almost every song on the album became an FM staple from the chain to second hand news to Gold Dust Woman."

podcast.title: Lindsey Buckingham's Departure in 1987
podcast.body: Toward the end of 1987, Lindsey Buckingham unexpectedly announced his departure from Fleetwood Mac, just weeks before the launch of a tour to support "Tango in the Night." This decision stemmed from his burnout after carrying the creative burden of the latest LP. "Toward the end of 1987, Buckingham stunned his fellow bandmates when, just weeks before the launch of a tour to support Tango, he announced he was leaving Fleetwood Mac, the result of his burnout after carrying their latest LP."

podcast.title: Lack of Appeal to Generation X (1990)
podcast.body: By 1990, the generation that had aged out of pop music from artists like New Kids on the Block was not interested in moving on to artists like Fleetwood Mac. "And they certainly weren't interested in moving on to Whitney Houston and Fleetwood Mac."

podcast.title: Christine McVie's Absence from 2003 Album
podcast.body: Christine McVie declined to fully rejoin Fleetwood Mac for their 2003 album "Say You Will," although she did contribute backing vocals to a few tracks, such as Lindsey Buckingham's "Believe To Love Her." "The one hold out was Christine McV, who declined to rejoin the band for Say You Will, but she did contribute backing vocals to a few tracks, such as Lindsay Buckingham's Believe To Love Her."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Christine McVie's Return to Live Performance in 2013
podcast.body: Christine McVie was finally persuaded to return to the stage in 2013 for a single, highly publicized appearance at London's O2 Arena. This event proved to be a "breakthrough" for her, leading to her rejoining the band and touring extensively with Fleetwood Mac in the final decade of her life. "It was only in 2013 that she was finally persuaded to return on stage for a much-touted single appearance at London's O2 Arena."

podcast.title: Lindsey Buckingham's Absence from 2019 Tour
podcast.body: Lindsey Buckingham was once again out of the band during Fleetwood Mac's final tour in 2019. "On that final 2019 tour, by the way, Lindsay Buckingham was once again out of the band."

podcast.title: Anti-convulsant Medication
podcast.body: Lindsey Buckingham of Fleetwood Mac needs to take anti-convulsant drugs, implying a condition such as epilepsy or a similar neurological disorder requiring such medication. "Lindsay Buckingham of Fleetwood Mac needs to take anti-convulsant drugs."

podcast.title: Band Burnout and Solo Projects Post-Tusk Tour
podcast.body: After an extensive 11-month tour supporting "Tusk," the band members experienced burnout with each other and eagerly pursued individual projects, leading to three out of the five members releasing solo albums in 1981. "After an 11-month tour supporting Tusk, the band members were burned out on each other and eager to work outside of Fleetwood Mac."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Band Members' Addiction During Tango in the Night
podcast.body: During the 18-month recording of "Tango in the Night," Mick Fleetwood was battling cocaine addiction, and Stevie Nicks went to rehab at the Betty Ford Clinic for her cocaine addiction. "He'd painstakingly compiled songs from fragments contributed by the other band members, including Mick Fleetwood, who was battling cocaine addiction, and especially Stevie Nicks, who actually went to rehab at the Betty Ford Clinic for her cocaine addiction."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Band Turnover - Pernicious Running Theme
podcast.body: A persistent and detrimental theme throughout Fleetwood Mac's history has been frequent band turnover, particularly evident after Peter Green's departure in 1970. This included members like Jeremy Spencer and Danny Kirwan leaving, highlighting the instability that Christine McVie helped to navigate. "But that was when another more pernicious running theme of Fleetwood Mac emerged. Band turnover."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Band's Last Tour and Christine McVie's Final Show
podcast.body: Fleetwood Mac's last tour took place in 2019, prior to the COVID-19 pandemic. Christine McVie's final performance was in late November 2019, almost exactly three years before her passing in late November 2022 due to a brief illness. "The band last toured in 2019, the year before the COVID-19 pandemic."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Buckingham and McVie Production Chemistry
podcast.body: Lindsey Buckingham and Christine McVie consistently worked well together in the studio, and "Tango in the Night" notably contained some of their most polished productions. "Buckingham and McVe had always worked well together, and Tango in the Night contained some of their most polished productions."

podcast.title: Christine McVie's Absence from 2000s Touring
podcast.body: Throughout the entire 2000s, while Fleetwood Mac toured frequently and lucratively, Christine McVie remained off stage. "but McV stayed off stage for all of the 2000's."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Christine McVie's Consistent Stage Presence and Anchoring Role
podcast.body: Christine McVie typically occupied a position behind her keyboards, singing slightly apart from the front of the stage. Her stage presence was described as unflashy, friendly, familiar, and reliable, underscoring her role in quietly anchoring Fleetwood Mac for nearly 50 years, with her songs consistently featured in the setlist. "Christine McV could usually be found behind her keyboards, singing slightly apart from the front of the stage."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Christine McVie's Initial Resistance to Solo Work
podcast.body: While other members of Fleetwood Mac ventured into solo careers after "Tusk," Christine McVie resisted the "solo siren song" for nearly a decade and a half, strategically saving her songs for the next Fleetwood Mac album, a decision that proved "wise." She had, however, been the first to release a solo LP back in 1970 under the name Christine Perfect. "The One Regular Mac songwriter, who resisted the solo siren song, was Christine McVeigh."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Christine McVie's Optimistic Songwriting
podcast.body: Christine McVie demonstrated an optimistic approach to songwriting about romantic difficulties, famously stating, "I'm just definitely not a pessimist," often transforming heartbreak into uplifting themes in her music. "When it came to writing about romantic travail, Christine later said, quote, I'm just definitely not a pessimist, unquote."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Christine McVie's Songwriting and Singing
podcast.body: Christine McVie was responsible for writing and singing a significant number of Fleetwood Mac's greatest songs. "Christine McVeebe, who wrote in saying a ton of Fleetwood Max greatest songs."

podcast.title: Christine McVie's Temporary Retirement from Touring
podcast.body: Christine McVie opted out of touring for the "Behind the Mask" album and temporarily retired from the road. "Christine McV turned down touring for behind the mask, even retiring temporarily from the road."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Classic Lineup Reunion by Presidential Decree
podcast.body: In the early 1990s, the classic Fleetwood Mac lineup reunited for a single performance at the request of US presidential candidate Bill Clinton. Clinton had adopted Christine McVie's song "Don't Stop" as his campaign theme, and as the new commander-in-chief, he requested the band, including Lindsey Buckingham, perform at his January 1993 inaugural. "The classic lineup did reunite for one gig in the early 90s, essentially by presidential decree."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Cocaine Use and Liner Note Credit Suggestion
podcast.body: The band experienced significant issues with cocaine, to the extent that they once considered giving their "Coke dealer" a credit in the album liner notes. "After all, this is a group that once thought about giving their Coke deal or credit on their albums, Liner Notes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Concert Attendance by Derek Whibley
podcast.body: Derek Whibley attended a Fleetwood Mac concert in late 2014 as part of his recovery process, seeking to reconnect with the music world after his health issues had prevented him from playing. "He knows going to see Aerosmith, I went to see Fleetwood Mac and a few things like that just to kind of get out and the only thing I wanted to do was go to a concert though."

podcast.body: In their early days, Fleetwood Mac was recognized as British blues rock hitmakers, a foundation from which Christine McVie's songwriting evolved. "their early days as British blues rock hitmakers..."

podcast.title: Early Digital Recording Efforts
podcast.body: Fleetwood Mac is cited as one of the groups who utilized early digital recording for their albums, reflecting the nascent stages of digital audio production where full end-to-end digital processing was not yet common. "There were plenty of other albums like that, Stevie Wonder, Christopher Cross, Fleetwood Mac, and a bunch of others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: End of Famed 5-Person Lineup
podcast.body: Lindsey Buckingham's departure in late 1987 permanently ended the famed five-person lineup (Buckingham, Mick Fleetwood, Christine McVie, John McVie, and Stevie Nicks) that had generated over a dozen years of hits, as they would never record a full studio album together again. "The famed 5-person Mac lineup, Buckingham, McFleetwood, Christine McVe, John McVe, and Stevie Nicks that had generated more than a dozen years of hits would never record a full studio album together again."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Fleetwood Mac's Perseverance
podcast.body: The history of Fleetwood Mac, tracing back to its 1960s founding by Peter Green, is characterized by "Perseverance," with Mick Fleetwood actively working to keep the band alive through various lineup changes. "But the story of Fleetwood Mac dating to the 1960s and its founding by Peter Green was one of Perseverance."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Infamous Drama - Fuel for Rumours Album
podcast.body: Fleetwood Mac is well-known for its infamous internal drama, characterized by fractious breakups, betrayals, recriminations, addictions, and soap opera-quality plot twists. This highly charged interpersonal conflict was a significant factor in making the 1977 *Rumours* album a blockbuster and has fueled nearly half a century of media hype. "This podcast episode is going to touch only lightly upon Fleetwood Mac's infamous drama, The Fractious Breakups, Betrayals, Recriminations, Addictions, and Soap Opera quality plot twists that helped make 1977's Rumors album A Blockbuster."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Influence on "Twice Removed"
podcast.body: Fleetwood Mac was among the artists Sloan members were listening to while creating "Twice Removed," contributing to the album's shift towards a quieter, more poppy sound. "I think some of the records that we're listening to more were like Fleetwood Mac or the third Velvet Underground album, which is sort of quieter records, you know."

podcast.title: Intense Songwriting Competition During Rumours
podcast.body: During the creation of "Rumours," Nicks, Buckingham, and Christine McVie were all vigorously spurring each other on to achieve "never better songwriting," both melodically and lyrically, which contributed to the album's exceptional quality. "Nicks, Buckingham and Christine McVeigh were all spurring each other to never better songwriting, melodically as well as lyrically."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Internal Relationship Drama and Drug Use Fueling Songwriting
podcast.body: During the mid-to-late 1970s, the band was immersed in intense personal drama, including a "messy love triangle" involving Stevie Nicks, Mick Fleetwood, and Lindsey Buckingham, simultaneous with the impending divorce of John and Christine McVie. This, combined with "a whole lot of drugs," provided the band "a lot of material to write about" for their songs, despite the personal challenge of having to perform together nightly. "It would not take long though for relationship drama Stevie and Mick and Stevie and Lindsey form a messy love triangle while the same time the McVees were on their way to divorce. You take that and a whole lot of drugs and you combine it and it gives the band a lot of material to write about if they could survive it and if they could stand to be near each other on the stage."

podcast.title: Intra-Band Relationships and Infidelity
podcast.body: During the recording of the Rumours album, it was widely known that members of Fleetwood Mac were involved in romantic and sexual relationships with each other. After exhausting these internal combinations, some members reportedly began relationships with people outside the band. "everybody seemed to be fooling around with everybody else. And when all those combinations were exhausted, members started missing around with people outside the band."

podcast.title: Late 70s Lineup Transformation
podcast.body: The addition of American members Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks in the late 1970s, alongside Christine McVie's existing songwriting prowess, significantly powered Fleetwood Mac's biggest LP, "Rumours," and subsequent success. "The Americans, Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks have joined the band. And their songs and McVees are going to power Fleetwood Mac's biggest LP ever."

podcast.body: For "Tango in the Night," Lindsey Buckingham took a full producer credit for the first time on a Fleetwood Mac album, reflecting his significant creative control over the project. "Buckingham even took a full producer credit for the first time on a Mac album."

podcast.title: Long Commercial Downturn - Early 1970s
podcast.body: After its early days as a bluesy guitar rock act, Fleetwood Mac experienced a long commercial downturn in the early 1970s. During this period, the band saw significant turnover, including Jeremy Spencer leaving to join a religious cult and Danny Kirwan being fired, with hit songs stopping on both sides of the Atlantic. "First as Fleetwood Mac was about to sink into a long commercial and professional wilderness period."

podcast.title: Making Rock More Palatable (1970s)
podcast.body: After its lineup changes, Fleetwood Mac's version of rock music broadened the genre's appeal, making it "more palatable to those who were no longer interested in Jimmy Hendrix or Led Zeppelin." "I do think that their version of rock made rock more palatable to those who were no longer interested in Jimmy Hendrix or Led Zeppelin."

podcast.title: Mellow Rock Trend (Early 1970s)
podcast.body: A "new look" Fleetwood Mac was cited as an example of artists popular in the early 1970s whose music contributed to the "Mellow" trend, as fans deserted the harder, more soulful sounds of the 60s for a softer approach. "The word everyone was using was Mellow, James Taylor, Bread, Olivia Newton John, Paul Simon, the California Rock of the Eagles, a new look Fleetwood Mac."

podcast.title: Most Successful, Best-Selling, Hit-Generating Group - Chart History
podcast.body: Fleetwood Mac is recognized as one of the most successful, best-selling, and hit-generating groups in chart history, largely due to a pivotal moment in the mid-70s when Stevie Nicks and Lindsey Buckingham joined, transforming them into multi-platinum superstars. However, their history also includes earlier periods of hit-making and resilience, significantly influenced by Christine McVie. "Fleetwood Mac are one of the most successful, best-selling and hit-generating groups in Chart History."

podcast.title: Musical Influences of Stevie Nicks
podcast.body: Stevie Nicks cited The Supremes and "amazing black musical groups who were top 40 when I was in the fourth grade" as key influences on her singing style, also mentioning songwriters Carol King, Gerry Goffin, Barry Mann, and Cynthia Weil. "I said to myself, there's that little girl that was singing along to the Supremes, all the amazing black musical groups who were top 40 when I was in the fourth grade, Carol and Jerry, Barry Man and Cynthia Wilde, those are all the songs that I learned to sing to."

podcast.title: Past Royalty Income as Retirement Annuity
podcast.body: In the "old days," groups like Fleetwood Mac could effectively retire because they reliably received large royalty checks every six months from sales of records they had released decades earlier. "And groups like the Eagles and Fleetwood Mac could retire because every six months or so. A big fat royalty check would arrive in the mail as the result of sales of records that they released decades earlier."

podcast.title: Post-Release Appreciation for *Rumours*' Flawlessness
podcast.body: Over time, *Rumours* has gained collective appreciation for its "near musical flawlessness," described as having "not a clunker in the mix." Its lyrics were deeply meaningful not only to the band members who lived the experiences but also to listeners, contributing to its enduring legacy. "Over time we collectively have come to appreciate the near musical flawlessness of this record not a clunker in the mix and how the lyrics were and are not just meaningful to them but to the listeners as well."

podcast.body: The lyrics on the *Rumours* album were described as "meaningful," "radio friendly," and "not aggressive," attributes that contributed to its widespread success and appeal. "The Lyrics, the meaningful, the songs, radio friendly, not aggressive."

podcast.title: Record for Four Top Ten Hits from One Album
podcast.body: The "Rumours" album set a historical record by becoming the first single artist LP in chart history to generate four top ten hits on the Hot 100. "When you make Loving Fun peaked at number nine in December 1977, rumors became the first single artist LP in chart history to generate four top ten hits."

podcast.title: Reunion for Touring
podcast.body: Fleetwood Mac was one of many bands from past decades that reunited in the 21st century, a trend largely motivated by financial incentives. With declining CD sales impacting artist revenues, returning to the touring circuit offered a lucrative way to appeal to nostalgic fan bases and fill large venues. "The list of reunions is long."

podcast.title: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame Acoustic Set
podcast.body: In 1998, during their induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, Fleetwood Mac performed an acoustic set that notably began with Christine McVie's classic 1976 hit "Say You Love Me," rather than any of the more prominent "Rumours" hits. "In 1998, when Fleetwood Mac were inducted into the rock and roll hall of fame, they performed an acoustic set that was led off, not by any of the big rumors hits, but rather Christine's classic 1976 hit Say You Love Me."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Romantic Breakups During Rumours Recording
podcast.body: Infamously, all five members of Fleetwood Mac experienced significant romantic breakups during the making of the "Rumours" album. This included John and Christine McVie's divorce in 1976 due to John's alcoholism and the strains of their shared life and work, the permanent splintering of Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks' relationship due to his controlling nature and her affair, and Mick Fleetwood's discovery of his wife Jenny Boyd's romantic involvement with former Fleetwood Mac guitarist Bob Weston, leading to multiple divorces. "Infamously, every member of Fleetwood Mac literally all five of them underwent some kind of romantic breakup during the making of rumors."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Rumours as an Exception in Chart History
podcast.body: Prior to "Rumours," no album by a single act had ever generated more than three top ten hits on the Hot 100, highlighting the album's unprecedented success. "To that date in Hot 100 history, no album by a single act had ever generated more than three top ten's."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: The Rumours Turmoil Legend
podcast.body: A widely discussed legend surrounding "Rumours" suggests that the intense emotional turmoil and "torturous" working conditions caused by the band members' romantic breakdowns actually enhanced the quality of the music. "The legend of rumors is that all this turmoil and the band members all agree that working together at this time was often torturous, made the music better."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Top-Selling Album in the 1970s with Female Artists
podcast.body: A review of top-selling albums from the 1970s reveals that 1977 was the only year where the top-selling album, `Rumours`, featured female artists, highlighting the rarity of such success for women in the era. "A quick perusal of the top selling albums for each year of the 1970s shows us that there was only one year where the top selling album had female artists in it. That was 1977 when Fleetwood Mac released rumors."

podcast.title: Transatlantic Band Formation
podcast.body: Fleetwood Mac formed as a transatlantic band, combining British and American members to forge its unique sound and appeal. "We talked about the formation of transatlantic band Fleetwood Mac..."

podcast.title: Transformation from Blues to Hitmaking Machine
podcast.body: Fleetwood Mac was originally a blues band before Stevie Nicks and Lindsey Buckingham joined. Their arrival "turn[ed] the direction of Fleetwood Mac around into what we generally think of Fleetwood Mac today, a hitmaking machine." "But when she and Lindsey joined Fleetwood Mac, Fleetwood Mac was most definitely a blues band."

srcs.source: For the Record - The 70s
For the Record - The 70s

podcast.title: Transformation into Multi-Platinum Superstars - Buckingham and Nicks Era
podcast.body: Fleetwood Mac was transformed into multi-platinum superstars after the mid-1970s arrival of singer-songwriter Stevie Nicks and guitarist/studio whiz Lindsey Buckingham. This moment is generally seen as central to their story, despite Christine McVie's consistent hit-making before and during this period. "When Nicks and Buckingham joined the group, they were indeed transformed into multi-platinum superstars."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Triumvirate Songwriting Approach - Stevie, Lindsey, Christine
podcast.body: Fleetwood Mac adopted a unique songwriting structure with three independent-minded singer-songwriters: Stevie Nicks, Lindsey Buckingham, and Christine McVie. This triumvirate approach, not common in many bands, heightened the group's drama and contributed to the highly charged perspectives expressed in their songs, drawing comparisons to The Beatles. "Not many bands take this triumvirate approach to songwriting, the structure of Fleetwood Mac heightened the band's drama."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Tusk Album's Anomaly for Christine McVie's Hits
podcast.body: "Tusk" stands out as the only LP during Fleetwood Mac's peak hitmaking period where Christine McVie did not write either the most or the biggest hits. "Tusk, which only reached number four on the album chart and sold a fraction of what rumors did, wound up the only LP of Fleetwood Mac's peak hitmaking period where Christine McVeigh didn't write either the most or the biggest hits."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Two Women in a Supergroup
podcast.body: The presence of two women, Stevie Nicks and Christine McVie, singing lead vocals and writing "incredible songs" in Fleetwood Mac was a significant achievement for its time, though often taken for granted today due to the band's enduring popularity. "The idea that two women would be in this rock supergroup and sing lead vocals and write these incredible songs is something that I think we all take for granted because Fleetwood Mac music is still everywhere."

xref.title: Derek Whibley's Recovery & Return to Music (2014)
xref.body: After his severe health crisis in May 2014, Derek Whibley embarked on a rigorous recovery, including daily physical therapy to regain his ability to walk and play guitar. By November 2014, he began writing music again and felt physically better. To reintegrate into the music world, he started attending concerts, including shows by Aerosmith and Fleetwood Mac, as he was unable to perform himself at the time. "I would say by November of 2014, I was starting to write music again and felt like I could kind of walk around, okay, and it was getting better."
